title: Etale lattice categories and pinned relative character reconstruction data
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Write $\mathbf Z^r_S$ for the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] of the finite free abelian group $\mathbf Z^r$, including $r=0$. A lattice is an abelian sheaf $M$ with an etale covering $\{U_i\to S\}$ and finite ranks $r_i$ such that $M|_{U_i}\simeq\mathbf Z^{r_i}_{U_i}$; ranks may vary and the base may be empty. Let $\operatorname{Lat}(S)$ be their full category. Let $\operatorname{Tor}(S)$ be the full category of commutative group objects over $S$ satisfying [def-sfb-relative-torus]. Use the Laurent Hopf split model $G_{r,S}$ and its coordinate from [def-sfb-relative-split-torus-laurent-model]. For a commutative $S$-group scheme $P$ and $T\to S$, define $C_P(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{T\text{-grp}}(P_T,G_{1,T})$, with pointwise multiplication; restriction is group-scheme base change [def-pc-base-change]. For an abelian sheaf $M$, a functional over $T$ is a morphism $M|_T\to\mathbf G_{m,T}$ in abelian sheaves, where restriction is ordinary inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the units sheaf is the $\mathbf G_m$ of [def-sc-gm-torsor]. Pull back functionals with the canonical comparison $g^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$, without requiring it to be invertible. Define a reconstruction datum to consist of: stability of tori and lattices under all base changes; for each $S$ an equivalence $E_S:\operatorname{Tor}(S)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\operatorname{Lat}(S)$; additive section equivalences $E_S(P)(U)\simeq C_P(U)$ respecting restriction and precomposition in $P$; additive point equivalences $D_S(M)(T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M|_T,\mathbf G_{m,T})$ natural in $T$ and contravariant in $M$, where $D_S$ is the inverse of $E_S$; the counit inverse given by $m\mapsto(h\mapsto h(m))$ and the opposite-unit inverse given by $p\mapsto(\chi\mapsto\chi(p))$, tested on every etale $U$ and every $U$-point. Include natural base-change comparisons for both functors, with character comparison normalized by pulling back characters and evaluating on points; impose the canonical identity and composition laws and require the dual comparison to be the counit mate of the character comparison. Finally require every base change trivializing $M$ with rank $r$ to identify $D_S(M)$ with $G_{r,T}$; require its structure morphism to be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], affine, flat and surjective, and locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; and require over every algebraically closed field-valued point a split fibre of the rank of the pulled-back lattice (equivalently the geometric stalk rank). This defines data and its conditions, and asserts no existence.
